start.text: The boathouse is cut into the foot of the cliff: a long low front of black stone, eight arched slips open to the water, a number chiselled over each. Seven of them are empty. Their rollers are still greased; the rails run down into the sea, and the weed has only just begun on them.

In the eighth slip a Keepers' boat sits on her rollers, tarred dark below a pale strake, with her oars shipped along the thwarts and her painter coiled on the bow. Ready. She has never been in the water.
Whoever she was kept for didn't come down to her.
Up there, somewhere. Up the stair, Merrit says.
